rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim favors Quraysh speech and then the nearest Mudar dialects because of their proximity to the Prophet’s birthplace and the place of revelation; he calls Rabiʿa and Mudar brothers.
rows.anchor: خص هؤلاء دون ربيعة وسائر العرب لقرب جوارهم من مولد النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم ومنزل الوحى

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik says the Qur’an is mostly in the Hijazi dialect, with a few Tamimi forms: assimilation is Tamimi, while preserving doubled consonants, as in فليملل and يحلل, is common in Hijaz.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ جمال الدين بن مالك أنزل الله القرآن بلغة الحجازيين إلا قليلا فإنه نزل بلغة التميميين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers unanimously put the disconnected exception in the accusative, following Hijazi usage; Banu Tamim instead allow it to follow the preceding expression.
rows.anchor: وأجمع القراء على نصب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats إلا الله in قل لا يعلم من في السماوات والأرض الغيب إلا الله as a disconnected exception in the Tamimi dialect; the excerpt says he was disputed but does not name the opponent.
rows.anchor: أنه استثناء منقطع جاء على لغة تميم ثم نازعه فى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed explanation reads the clause by meaning: من is singular in form but can refer to two, so the following dual expression is licensed.
rows.anchor: أنه كلام محمول على المعنى أي فإن كان من ترك اثنتين وهذا مفيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer treats the dual form as an old construction whose usual pattern had been abandoned; the Qur’an preserves other such forms, including استحوذ.
rows.anchor: الثاني ان يكون من الاشياء التي جاءت على اصولها المرفوضة

rows.speaker: ابن الضائع النحوي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Da’i says the meaning is “two or more,” with the lowest number standing for it and all greater numbers.
rows.anchor: المراد فان كانتا اثنتين فصاعدا فعبر بالأدنى عنه وعما فوقه قال ابن الضائع النحوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فإن لم يكونا رجلين, the dual witnesses are understood from the pronoun and the preceding شهيدين; رجلين can be read as a circumstantial phrase, as in وضعتها أنثى.
rows.anchor: فإن الرجولية المثناة فهمت من الضمير بدليل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An objection says يكونا already refers to the two male witnesses, since شهيدين was restricted to men, making the wording appear to say “if the two men are not men.”
rows.anchor: وأورد بعضهم السؤال في الاول فقال الضمير في

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: A response attributed to al-Akhfash says the predicate gives bare number without a quality; the author calls it weak because رجلين for اثنين is a remote figurative substitution.
rows.anchor: بما اجاب به الاخفش في آية المواريث ان الخبر هنا افاد العدد المجرد عن الصفة وهذا ضعيف

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi says what is stripped away is a quality such as masculinity or femininity; the author objects that this still does not explain why the wording states number already carried by the dual pronoun.
rows.anchor: والذي ذكره الفارسي المجرد منهما الرجولية أو الانوثية أو غيرها من الصفات

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some parse رجلين as an explanatory circumstantial accusative with complete kāna; the author says this answers a question about parsing, not the rhetorical arrangement, and adds needless strain.
rows.anchor: منصوب على الحال المبينة وكان تامه فهو اظرف من الاول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s preferred reading takes شهيدين as two witnesses of either sex, then qualifies them as men; the pronoun returns to the unqualified pair, so the condition negates their being men and fits the fallback.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر في جواب السؤال هو ان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inheritance verse, the dual pronoun replaces the explicit الوارث for brevity, even without a prior verbal antecedent; this also avoids awkwardly reporting a dual predicate about a singular-form noun, as in village for its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: فكأنه قال فإن كان الوارث اثنين ثم وضع ضمير الاثنين موضع الوارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stating a qualification can distinguish a special case within its class even when omitted cases share the rule; the author gives several rhetorical benefits for such specification.
rows.anchor: لتخصيص الشيء بالذكر فوائد منها اختصاصه في جنسه بشيء لا يشركه فيه غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intentional killing is singled out because the verse’s concluding divine retaliation applies to deliberate killing, not accidental killing.
rows.anchor: إن المتعمد إنما خص بالذكر لما عطف عليه في آخر الآية من الإنتقام

words: فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِى ٱلْحَجِّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prohibition may name sacred months or pilgrimage to honor those settings, although the prohibited conduct is forbidden at all times.
rows.anchor: فخص النهى عن الظلم فيهن وإن كان الظلم منهيا عنه في جميع الأوقات تفضيلا لهذه الأشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A condition can describe the usual situation: stepdaughters commonly live in their mothers’ care, though the wording identifies the prevalent case.
rows.anchor: فإن الغالب من حال الربيبة أنها تكون في حجر أمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three named times for servants to seek permission are singled out because bodily exposure is usual then, without excluding other times when privacy is needed.
rows.anchor: خص هذه الأوقات الثلاثة بالاستئذان لأن الغالب تبذل البدن فيهن

words: فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear that the spouses will not keep God’s limits is stated as the usual context for a wife’s redemption in divorce; it does not confine the ruling to that circumstance.
rows.anchor: فالافتداء يجوز مع الأمر وقوله

words: إِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَن تَقْصُرُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear is named with shortening prayer as a prevalent circumstance, an example of qualifying a ruling by its common context.
rows.anchor: فليس عليكم جناح أن تقصروا من الصلاة إن خفتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fallback of one man and two women is another example in the discussion of specifying circumstances in a legal rule.
rows.anchor: فإن لم يكونا رجلين فرجل وامرأتان

words: وَإِن كُنتُمْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ وَلَمْ تَجِدُوا۟ كَاتِبًا فَرِهَٰنٌ مَّقْبُوضَةٌ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The author says travel is named because a scribe is commonly unavailable then; this does not support Mujahid’s view that pledges are allowed only during travel.
rows.anchor: لأن الكاتب إنما يعدم غالبا فيه ولا يدل على منع الرهن إلا في السفر كما صار إليه مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author lists Qur’anic denunciations as signs that an act is forbidden, including calling it injustice, wrongful appropriation, sin, or fisq, as in the ban on harming scribes and witnesses.
rows.anchor: أو وصف بخبث أو رجس أو بخس أو بكونه فسقا أو إثما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A divine question about why people perform an act signals blame when no answer is supplied; if an answer follows, the legal implication depends on that answer.
rows.anchor: وسؤاله سبحانه عن علة الفعل نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On an adjectival parse, إلا is like غير rather than an exception; this avoids treating God as either a member of the gods’ genus or an unrelated exception.
rows.anchor: وإذا جعل وصفا فقد امن فيه مخالفة الجنس ف إلا هي بمنزلة غير لا بمعنى الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If إلا أنفسهم is exceptional, it is out of kind: the accused’s own selves are not the required witnesses to adultery, and his oath does not nullify the testimony; an adjectival reading avoids this issue.
rows.anchor: فلو كان استثناء لكان من غير الجنس لان انفسهم ليس شهودا على الزنا

rows.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Qahir calls the preceding argument baseless: it would make إلا an exception or adjective in other verses where neither analysis is accepted, and an adjective should match the described word’s case.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ عبد القاهر الجرجاني هذا توهم منه وخاطر خطر من غير اصل

rows.speaker: المبرد والجرمي
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Jarmi say a nominative reading قليل would be sound as an adjective after a disconnected exception.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد والجرمي في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن الضائع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Da’i reads إلا الله as بدل or عوض, meaning “instead of Allah,” which avoids the familiar problem of exception or adjectival readings.
rows.anchor: وجعل ابن الضائع منه

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik takes إلا الله as an adjective for emphasis, not specification, since the existence of multiple gods would entail corruption even without it.
rows.anchor: بقي إن يقال إن ابن مالك جعلها في الاية صفة وأنها للتأكيد لا للتخصيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Ibn Malik’s emphasis reading: آلهة can mean a genus or plurality, so إلا الله specifies that corruption follows plurality; likewise اثنين restricts إلهين to make the prohibition of two explicit.
rows.anchor: فلو اقتصر عليه لتوهم إن الفساد مرتب على الجنس

rows.speaker: شيخ المالكية
rows.claim: The Maliki shaykh forbids anomalous readings in prayer or elsewhere, even for readers ignorant of Arabic; the uninformed are taught, while knowing or persistent readers are disciplined.
rows.anchor: وقال شيخ المالكية رحمه الله لا يجوز أن يقرأ بالقراءة الشاذة فى صلاة ولا غيرها عالما بالعربية كان أو جاهلا

rows.speaker: شيخ المالكية
rows.claim: He says replacing Qur’anic words such as آتينا and سولت with synonyms is not a variant reading but an even graver offense, deserving stronger discipline and prohibition.
rows.anchor: وأما تبديل آتينا بأعطينا وسولت بزينت ونحوه فليس هذا من الشواذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Maliki shaykh prefers not to combine different canonical readings in one verse; combining forms where one reading depends on the other, including this phrase with فتذكر in the accusative, is prohibited under the same ruling.
rows.anchor: مثل أن يقرأ نغفر لكم بالنون وخطيئاتكم بالجمع

rows.speaker: الشيخ شهاب الدين
rows.claim: Shihab al-Din permits combining readings when they do not depend on one another, citing the seven ahruf as a concession; he sees no harm in such combinations.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ شهاب الدين والمنع من هذا ظاهر وأما ما ليس كذلك فلا يمنع منه فإن الجمع جائز

rows.speaker: الشيخ شهاب الدين
rows.claim: Shihab al-Din dislikes repeatedly reciting a verse with different readings as some contemporaries do during a Qur’an completion, calling it an innovation without early precedent.
rows.anchor: نعم أكره ترداد الآية بقراءات مختلفة كما يفعله أهل زماننا فى جمع القرآن

rows.speaker: النووي عن أصحاب الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi reports the Shafi‘i jurists’ view that anomalous readings are not Qur’an because they lack mass transmission, so reciting them in prayer or elsewhere is forbidden.
rows.anchor: نقله النووى فى شرح المهذب عن أصحاب الشافعى فقال قال أصحابنا وغيرهم لا تجوز القراءة فى الصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن عبد البر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr transmits Muslim consensus that anomalous readings may not be recited and that one should not pray behind someone who uses them.
rows.anchor: ونقل ابن عبد البر إجماع المسلمين على أنه لا تجوز القراءة بالشواذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An action may be attributed to the time in which it occurs, as in the Day making children gray; alternatively, the phrase can elide that the Day’s terror makes them gray.
rows.anchor: نسب الفعل إلى الظرف لوقوعه فيه

words: مَا لِىٓ أَدْعُوكُمْ إِلَى ٱلنَّجَوٰةِ وَتَدْعُونَنِىٓ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people called the believer to disbelief, not literally to Hell; Hell names the consequence of the disbelief, as the following words clarify.
rows.anchor: وهم لم يدعوه إلى النار إنما دعوه إلى الكفر بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A consequence can stand for its cause: fear of Fire means shun defiance, eating orphan property entails Fire, consuming wealth by falsehood means gambling, and al-rijz means idol worship that causes punishment.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فاتقوا النار ﴾ أي العناد المستلزم للنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وليستعفف الذين لا يجدون نكاحا, nikāḥ means the resources required to marry, such as the dower, maintenance, and other necessary funds.
rows.anchor: انما ارد والله اعلم الشيء الذي ينكح به من مهر ونفقة ومالا بد للمتزوج منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is phrased as making enemies find severity to show that their perception is the intended outcome; severity itself is a means, not an end.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على انه المقصود لذاته وأما الإغلاظ فلم يقصد لذاته بل لتجدوه

words: فَٱعْتَدُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا ٱعْتَدَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conversely, a result can be named by its cause: just retaliation is called an evil or aggression after the opponent’s wrongdoing, and God’s punishment is called a plot because their plot caused it; a genuinely painful act is literal, not this trope.
rows.anchor: سمي الجزاء الذي هو السبب سيئة واعتداء فسمي الشيء باسم سببه

words: أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two women serve to ensure reminder, not to cause error; since forgetting triggers the other’s reminder, the cause is put in place of the intended outcome.
rows.anchor: إنما جعلت المرأتان للتذكير إذا وقع الضلال لا ليقع الضلال فلما كان الضلال سببا للتذكير أقيم مقامه

words: وَٱمْرَأَةً مُّؤْمِنَةً إِن وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَهَا لِلنَّبِىِّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says امرأة مؤمنة للنبي rather than لك, since a pronoun might suggest the permission applied to others too; the explicit wording marks the Prophet’s special privilege.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل لك لانه لو أتى بالضمير لأخذ جوازه لغيره

rows.speaker: عز الدين ابن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salam lists attention to cognate wordplay as a reason for explicit wording, illustrated by Sūrat al-Nās.
rows.anchor: ذكره الشيخ عز الدين ابن عبد السلام رحمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An explicit noun may be used to carry a pronoun that must be supplied, as in the repeated أهل in the story of Moses and his companion.
rows.anchor: أن يتحمل ضميرا الابد منه كقوله

words: أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating إحداهما instead of using a pronoun gives the noun greater importance and balances the two clauses; the author calls this rare structural or semantic parallelism, beyond mere sound-patterning.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إنما أعيد ﴿ إحداهما ﴾ لتعادل الكلم

words: أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ
rows.speaker: أبو الفتح عن المتنبي
rows.claim: Al-Fath recounts asking al-Mutanabbi whether he wrote قرحى or قرحا; al-Mutanabbi chose the latter because the following بهارا is a plural, an example of deliberate balance in wording.
rows.anchor: وقد استغرب أبو الفتح ما حكى عن المتنبي في قوله

words: أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse has parallel clauses for error and reminder; repeating the subject before the second action preserves its form and lets the clause close with balanced structure, while الأخرى clarifies the intended contrast.
rows.anchor: وبيان ما ذكرت في الاية أنها متضمنه لقسمين قسم الظلال وقسم التذكير

words: فَلَا يَحْزُنكَ قَوْلُهُمْ إِنَّا نَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ
وَلَا يَحْزُنكَ قَوْلُهُمْ إِنَّ ٱلْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses beginning إنا or إن العزة are not part of the opponents’ speech; they explain why their words should not grieve the Prophet, so the pause follows قولهم.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا من قولهم لأنه لو كان قولهم لما حزن الرسول وإنما جيء بالجملة لبيان العلة والسبب

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The source gives two parses: the request for protection is justified because the Fire is inescapable and a bad dwelling, or ساءت مستقرا ومقاما explains why its torment is inescapable.
rows.anchor: وفيها وجهان لأهل المعاني أحدهما أن سؤالهم لصرف العذاب معلل بأنه غرام

words: أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ
rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans explain an before a future verb as لئلا, “lest,” in examples such as أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر.
rows.anchor: أحدهما للكوفيين أن المعنى لئلا يقولوا ولئلا تقول نفس

words: أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ
rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans instead posit an omitted verbal noun or object, such as كراهة or حذار, before the clause.
rows.anchor: الثاني للبصريين أن المفعول محذوف أي كراهة أن يقولوا أو حذار أن يقولوا

words: أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ
rows.speaker: سيبويه والبصريون
rows.claim: For this verse, neither “lest one err” nor “for fear of error” makes error a sensible purpose of testimony; the intended purpose is reminder if one forgets, with error as its trigger, like preparing a prop to support a wall if it leans.
rows.anchor: فإن المقصود إذكار إحداهما الأخرى إذا ضلت نسيت فلما كان الضلال سببا للإذكار

words: أَفَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares repeated expressions in these verses as general and particular formulations, illustrating how adjoining clauses can reuse a term with different scope.
rows.anchor: فالاول عام والثاني خاص

words: لَخَلْقُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ خَلْقِ ٱلنَّاسِ
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired statements about creation and divine favor are further examples in the discussion of how a repeated wording can shift between general and particular scope.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فالحق والحق أقول, the first الحق is accusative as an oath and the second is the object of أقول; this differs from the two prepositional phrases in وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل.
rows.anchor: فالاول نصب على القسم والثاني نصب ب اقول وهذا بخلاف قوله

words: وَمَآ أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِىٓ إِنَّ ٱلنَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌۢ بِٱلسُّوٓءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وما أبرئ نفسي إن النفس, the first noun is specific and the second general; the first instance falls within the second.
rows.anchor: فالاول معرفة بالضمير والثانية عامة والاولى خاصة فالاول داخل في الثاني

words: عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other examples repeat a broad noun then specify it: سبيل الله, رب العالمين with رب موسى وهارون, and the general causes followed by the causes of the heavens.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ برب العالمين رب موسى وهارون ﴾

words: شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source describes the first wording as particular and the repeated wording as general, while both retain the same genus, as with God’s custom and Ramadan/the month.
rows.anchor: فهما وان اختلفا يكون الاول خاصا والثاني عاما متفقان بالجنس

words: إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِى مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ شَيْـًٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause confirms that the rejection of following conjecture is unrestricted: conjecture does not avail against truth at all.
rows.anchor: ولذلك استبدل بها على إن الاصل الغاء الظن مطلقا

words: أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated إحداهما may refer to the same woman or another; in 2:282, if the second is an object, definite nouns identify the same referent, while if it is subject they may match by kind. Most grammarians treat an unmarked first noun as subject, unlike al-Zajjaj’s view on دعواهم.
rows.anchor: فان كانت احداهما الثانية مفعولا فالاسم الاول هو الثاني على قاعدة المعرفتين

rows.speaker: السيرافي
rows.claim: Al-Sirafi says أن explains a command rather than direct speech, because a command contains the meaning of speech; he illustrates this with Jesus’ statement about worshipping God.
rows.anchor: وقال السيرافي ليست لإن تفسيرا للقول بل للقول بل للامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An may be extra after temporal لما; it is absent in the parallel wording about Lot, while its use before the bearer of good news suits the long wait and extended sorrow.
rows.anchor: الرابع زائدة وتكون بعد لما التوقيتية كقوله تعالى

words: وَمَا لَنَآ أَلَّا نُقَٰتِلَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says extra أن can still put the following verb in the subjunctive; the source compares examples with ألا to the parallel wording without أن.
rows.anchor: وذهب الاخفش إلى انها قد تنصب الفعل وهي مزيدة

words: أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ
rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans analyze أن in the witness verse as conditional; the following ف is their evidence for that reading.
rows.anchor: الخامس شرطية في قول الكوفيين

words: أَن يُؤْتَىٰٓ أَحَدٌ مِّثْلَ مَآ أُوتِيتُمْ
rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad connects أن يؤتى to ولا تؤمنوا إلا لمن تبع دينكم, treating the lām as extra; the source rejects this as the correct analysis.
rows.anchor: وزعم المبرد إن يؤتى متصل بقوله

words: أَن يُؤْتَىٰٓ أَحَدٌ مِّثْلَ مَآ أُوتِيتُمْ
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view places إن يؤتى in the nominative; the author instead identifies it as a مصدرية construction.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن يؤتى في موضع رفع

words: أَن يُؤْتَىٰٓ أَحَدٌ مِّثْلَ مَآ أُوتِيتُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s preferred analysis of أن يؤتى is مصدرية, rather than a negative أن or a clause joined to ولا تؤمنوا.
rows.anchor: والصحيح انها مصدرية

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: In purpose clauses such as يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا, the Basrans supply an omitted noun, كراهة, before أن; the sense is “lest you go astray.”
rows.anchor: وقال البصريون على حذف مضاف أي كراهة أن تضلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source gives أن the sense إذ with a past verb, though it also reports a causal reading for بل عجبوا أن جاءهم; with a present verb it reports “when you believe,” but prefers مصدرية.
rows.anchor: الثامن بمعنى اذ مع الماضي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows أن to substitute for a time adverb like ما, and cites Ibrahim’s debate with the king after God gave him sovereignty.
rows.anchor: واجاز الزمخشري إن تقع إن مثل ما
